assertion.text: For the same nonempty resource, a 200 GET response carries more body bytes than a 200 HEAD response under the 2022 HTTP standard worldwide.

result.scope_note: The claim is fully specified with respect to the HTTP methods, response code, resource condition (nonempty), timeframe (2022), and geographic scope (worldwide). The 2022 HTTP standard (RFC 9110) explicitly defines that HEAD responses must have the same headers as GET but never include a body, making this verifiable from the standard.

explanation.text: RFC 9110 requires that a HEAD response must not include a message body, even though it includes headers describing what would have been sent.
The headers in a 200 HEAD response, such as Content-Length, reflect the body that would have been sent in a 200 GET response for the same resource.
Because the GET response includes the actual body and the HEAD response omits it, the GET response carries more body bytes than the HEAD response.

excerpts.text: RFC 9110 says a server must not send a message body in a HEAD response — only the headers.

RFC 9110 defines HEAD as identical to GET except the server must not include a response body. The headers like Content-Length still describe the body that would have been returned for a GET, but the actual body is omitted.
